specification.objective: Correct Flutter Web browser history across TouchIn workspace screens, so Back restores the screen the user actually visited and navigation retains deep links and authentication boundaries.

requirements.statement: Workspace drawer navigation between main screens must preserve previous screen entries in the browser and Flutter route histories; using Back after A -> B returns to A, and Forward can return to B when the browser supports it.
Repeated selection of the already-active named workspace screen must not accumulate duplicate history entries; closing the drawer must not accidentally pop the screen.

Main named routes (/time-clock, /admin/employees, /admin/audit, /projects, /kanban, /settings) must continue to render their intended screens through the existing startup session guard and direct deep links.
The unauthenticated, expired/revoked session, required password change, error/retry and logout flows must retain their existing guards; Back must not expose protected workspace content after logout.
Retain the exact locked POLIS contract in docs/contracts/browser-navigation-history-issue-65-v1.polis.json, within its own allowed change scope.
The main audit workspace route must mount and render under AppTheme without unbounded button width layout failures; preserve the existing design and filtering actions.

An authenticated transition from login or registration must install a named, canonical workspace route in browser history; returning to that screen by browser Back must restore the matching browser URL as well as its content.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Regression navigates through distinct named workspace entries A -> B -> C, then invokes browser-style system Back twice and observes B then A, including correct route-update notifications.
Regression repeats a navigation item for the current named route, then invokes Back and verifies the previous screen rather than a duplicate.
Existing bootstrap/deep-link and logout widget tests plus the Flutter suite and web build continue to pass, including session error/retry behavior.
The locked contract is archived byte-for-byte in docs/contracts, and POLIS policy/contract checks pass for the implemented scope.
A logged-in deep-link widget mounts /admin/audit with the production theme without layout exceptions, as do the five other main routes.
A test simulates authenticated login replacement, verifies that browser route information publishes the canonical named destination and ensures browser Back after navigation restores its URL.

invariants.statement: Role-dependent default workspace and authentication flows retain their current security semantics.
The route names, screen widgets, theming and all API interfaces remain unchanged.
Navigation uses Flutter Navigator and the existing drawer architecture, without injecting JavaScript browser-history entries or adding dependencies.

forbidden_states.statement: Switching between different workspace menu destinations discards the preceding workspace screen from history.
Repeatedly selecting an already-open named screen creates phantom history entries.
Using Back after logout reveals protected content or bypasses required password changes.
The audit page produces an infinite-width layout exception on its primary toolbar when accessed via a named route.
Browser Back displays the previous workspace content while leaving the URL of the subsequent page due to an unnamed login destination.

inputs.statement: User selects primary workspace drawer destinations and uses browser Back/Forward or Flutter's system Back.
An authenticated, unauthenticated, revoked, or mandatory-password-change session at a supported direct URL.

outputs.statement: Consistent route stack and browser navigation history for named workspace destinations.
Regression tests and the archived immutable POLIS contract in the repository.

failure_semantics.statement: On the locked baseline, a widget regression must fail when browser-style Back cannot return from the selected workspace destination to its predecessor. It will print the marker workspace_back_history_missing upon failure.

argv: import subprocess,sys; p=subprocess.run(['flutter','test','test/features/shared/presentation/widgets/workspace_shell_test.dart','--plain-name','browser Back restores the previous workspace screen'],cwd='frontend'); print('workspace_back_history_missing' if p.returncode else 'workspace_back_history_present'); sys.exit(p.returncode)
